# Bluefin Tuna LLC — Project Planning Service Terms

**Version:** service-terms-2026-10-30-v2  
**Effective date:** 2026-10-30  
**Provider:** Bluefin Tuna LLC  
**Contact:** support@bluefintuna.life  
**Business correspondence address:** 1209 Mountain Road Pl NE, STE N, Albuquerque, NM 87110, USA



## 1. Provider, orders and application

These terms govern custom project-planning and project-controls services supplied by Bluefin Tuna LLC. The service provider and contracting seller is Bluefin Tuna LLC. Payments are processed through Stripe; paying through Stripe does not make Stripe the supplier of our planning services.

These standard online services are intended for business or professional use. A person placing a business order confirms that they are authorized to act for the named customer. A sole proprietor may purchase for their business. A purchaser's business-use declaration does not remove mandatory rights that apply to the actual transaction. Consumer requests requiring different disclosures or cancellation arrangements are reviewed before payment is accepted.

Your order consists of the accepted package, compatible add-ons, activity allowance, reporting period where relevant, input requirements, price, tax treatment, deliverables and revision allowance shown in the order summary or written quotation; these Service Terms; and our Cancellation & Refund Policy. Individually agreed written terms prevail for the identified order where lawful. Our Privacy Policy describes data handling separately.

An order is accepted when we confirm its scope and payment conditions through the portal or in writing. Payment confirmation alone does not mean that project inputs have been accepted as complete or that the delivery clock has started. If we cannot accept or supply a paid order, we will explain the issue and provide the remedy described in the Refund Policy.

These terms do not amend the terms for our App Store applications or unrelated software products. Planning purchases are not subscriptions unless separately and expressly agreed.

## 2. Packages and deliverables

Each main package covers one project. A Schedule Update covers one reporting period and one agreed data date. Prices below are in USD before any applicable transaction tax disclosed at checkout. The purchased order snapshot records the applicable price and scope.

| Service | Base price | Base activity allowance | Target turnaround | Main deliverables |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Primavera P6 Schedule Audit | $199 | 150 | 5 business days | PDF findings report; no corrected XER |
| Basic Baseline — Without Resources | $499 | 75 | 5 business days | XER and PDF |
| Basic Baseline — With Resources | $799 | 75 | 7 business days | XER and PDF |
| Detailed Baseline — Without Resources | $999 | 200 | 10 business days | XER, PDF and Excel output |
| Detailed Baseline — With Resources | $1,499 | 200 | 12 business days | XER, PDF and Excel output |
| Primavera P6 Schedule Update — Without Resources | $399 | 200 | 4 business days | Updated XER and PDF |
| Primavera P6 Schedule Update — With Resources | $649 | 200 | 5 business days | Updated XER and PDF |

Basic Baseline includes one in-scope revision; Detailed Baseline includes two. Schedule Update revision allowances are stated in the accepted order. Audits provide findings, not correction revisions. Correction of a material failure to meet the agreed scope is handled under the Refund Policy and is not automatically sold as an extra revision.

A separately offered **Primavera P6 Schedule Score — Pilot**, when enabled, is a genuine limited human-delivered service: one project, up to 150 activities, a basic one-page PDF scorecard and a target of five business days after accepted complete inputs. Its pilot price is $1 before any applicable tax. It is not a detailed audit, certified methodology or automated analysis guarantee. The scope and review method must be available when offered; a catalogue listing alone does not make the pilot available for purchase.

## 3. Additional activities, revisions and materials

Additional activity allowance is purchased in blocks of **up to 50** activities beyond the main package. An extra 1–50 activities is one block; 51–100 is two. Basic Baseline supports up to two added blocks, and Detailed Baseline and Schedule Update up to four. Larger scopes require a quotation. Audit and Score pilot packages do not accept these automatic add-ons.

The block prices are $100 without resources; $175 for Baseline with labor man-hours and cost allocation; and $150 for Update with existing labor man-hour and cost allocation. Additional in-scope revisions are $99 each, up to three subject to scope approval. Added activities or changed scope can affect turnaround; the adjusted date must be disclosed and agreed rather than silently extending the original commitment.

“With Resources” means labor man-hours and cost allocation based on client-supplied approved information. Physical material resources, equipment-hour models, independent estimates, quantity takeoff, BOQ creation, procurement and budget or unit-rate development are excluded unless separately agreed.

Material add-ons are separately selected for concrete (m³), reinforcement steel (metric tons), formwork (m²), structural steel (metric tons), and piping (meters or metric tons as agreed). Each category costs $249 for Baseline loading or $119 for updating existing assignments for one reporting period. The limit is **50 client-supplied BOQ rows per category**, not 50 physical units. Each selected category must fit the approved activity limit of its parent order.

Material add-ons require a compatible With Resources main package. Update material assignments require operator verification of existing mapping before payment. New resource dictionaries or first-time loading are not included in an Update price. Add-ons are not independent services unless expressly quoted against an identified existing project.

## 4. Information supplied by the customer

You supply complete, accurate and lawfully shared project information required by the purchased scope. This may include the P6 XER, baseline, BOQ or itemized work descriptions, quantities and units, drawings/specifications, constraints, calendars, milestone dates, progress measurements, data date, approved man-hour and cost budgets, actuals, forecasts and relevant unit rates.

Providing the BOQ, work items, measurements, budgets and applicable unit rates is your responsibility. We do not independently verify those quantities or create an estimate unless the order expressly includes that service. You remain responsible for business, engineering and site decisions based on the deliverables.

Use only the file formats accepted by the secure intake interface. Availability of an XLSX final deliverable does not mean that XLSX customer uploads are supported. For a restricted intake format, provide a supported CSV or PDF export or agree another secure method before payment. Do not send confidential project files through public links or unapproved email attachments.

Remove unnecessary personal identifiers, bank/card information, credentials, health data and unrelated third-party data. Do not submit material you lack permission to share, malicious content, or regulated/restricted material without prior written approval. Additional confidentiality, processing or security requirements must be agreed before documents are uploaded.

## 5. Delivery clock and changes

Turnaround begins only when required inputs are received and usable, the scope is accepted, and the agreed payment condition has been satisfied. The portal or written confirmation records the start and target delivery date. Unless the order specifies a different calendar, business days are Monday through Friday measured in UTC, excluding closure dates disclosed before acceptance.

Missing, contradictory or revised information may pause the work. We will explain the missing information and its effect on timing. We do not use a pause to remove your cancellation or remedy rights. If an extension, extra activity allowance, new reporting period or new resource mapping is needed, its price and timing must be agreed before the additional work is charged or performed.

Published turnaround is tied to the accepted scope. We will inform you promptly of a material delay and offer a reasonable revised arrangement or the remedy required by the order and applicable law. Our travel or connectivity arrangements do not create an undisclosed exemption from our obligations.

## 6. Payment, billing and taxes

Prices are one-time USD charges for the stated scope. The final amount and any collected tax are disclosed before payment. You must provide accurate billing identity, address, business-use information, project location and relevant tax identification where needed. A VAT/tax ID or a business label does not automatically make every transaction tax-exempt.

Applicable sales tax, VAT, GST or similar transaction taxes are determined from the relevant rules and the transaction facts. A no-tax, exempt or reverse-charge treatment is applied only where appropriate. Where the tax position cannot be determined before payment, acceptance may remain under review without charging you. We do not add undisclosed tax after you have agreed to a different total without addressing the change with you.

Stripe may perform additional fraud or payment authentication. We do not receive your full card number or security code. A successful redirect alone is not payment confirmation; the portal verifies the payment through Stripe. We distinguish a payment receipt from a tax invoice and provide the billing documentation appropriate to the transaction.

## 7. Revisions and project use

Included revisions address reasonable feedback within the original scope and information basis. New project areas, additional activities, changed budgets, another reporting period, recovery planning, new mappings and expert claims analysis are changes of scope. The order identifies revision allowances and any agreed feedback window. A missed informal feedback window does not waive mandatory rights concerning a defective or incomplete deliverable.

You retain rights in your original project documents. On payment of the agreed fee, we grant you a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use, copy, modify and share the delivered project-specific files for the project and your legitimate internal business purposes, including with the project's employer, contractor, advisers and other authorized stakeholders. Pre-existing methods, generic templates and tools remain ours or their respective owners'. No software licence for Primavera P6 or third-party products is included. Any broader ownership transfer is agreed separately in writing.

## 8. Intake, working storage and delivery access

Files first enter private Cloudflare R2 temporary intake. **New access to intake files ends 12 hours after the upload session is created**, whether paid or unpaid. Scheduled cleanup removes the objects after their expiry; physical removal can occur later than the access cutoff, particularly during incidents. Payment does not restart this clock.

After verified payment, necessary inputs may be copied to our private, access-controlled Google Drive project workspace to perform the service. That working copy is separate from R2 intake and is not erased simply because the 12-hour R2 period ends. We verify transfers and handle failures through retries, review or an authorized re-upload without charging for the same service again.

Approved final files are provided through the Bluefin Tuna customer portal, not a public Drive sharing link. Customers do not need a Google account. Only approved deliverables are exposed; internal working folders and credentials are not shared.

The normal final-delivery availability period is **30 days from publication of the approved final delivery**. The related private project workspace and final-file archive are scheduled for deletion **90 days from that same publication time**. Publication and expiry are shown in the portal. Downloading or opening an invitation does not automatically restart these periods. A materially revised final release has explicitly stated dates; archival deadlines are not silently reset by minor link reissues.

An unpublished project closed by cancellation or inability to proceed is normally scheduled for project-file deletion 30 days after written closure, unless a shorter lawful period or a documented preservation need applies. These project-file rules are separate from required accounting, agreement, security and dispute records, as explained in the Privacy Notice.

Please download the final files before access expires. A link may be single-use for establishing an authorized session; this does not mean that receipt of a technical download is acceptance of the quality of the work. If access fails during the availability period, contact support for secure assistance. Revocation or expiration does not remove accrued statutory rights.

## 9. Confidentiality, security and service limits

We restrict project documents to authorized personnel and service providers who need them to perform, secure or support the service. We do not publish customer project files or use them as public examples without separate permission. The Privacy Notice identifies the main providers and retention approach.

We use access controls and format/size checks and follow a controlled document-handling process. No security system is an absolute guarantee. A checksum confirms that bytes match; it is not a certification that a file is safe or professionally accurate.

Schedules and reports depend on the supplied information and assumptions. They do not guarantee completion by a certain date, recovery of delay, employer or authority approval, contractual entitlement, funding, productivity or any other project outcome. Legal advice, delay claims, extension-of-time opinions, independent quantity certification and regulated engineering approvals are outside the standard scope unless separately agreed and lawfully supplied.

## 10. Cancellation, remedies and disputes

Our Cancellation & Refund Policy forms part of the agreement. It provides a full-refund approach before work begins and a fair, documented calculation for cancellations after work begins, with remedies for work that materially fails to meet the agreed scope. Mandatory rights are not excluded.

Please first contact support@bluefintuna.life with the order reference so that we can investigate and seek a practical resolution. This contact process does not prevent lawful urgent remedies or require you to abandon a payment dispute or statutory deadline.

For business-to-business orders, these terms are governed by the laws of the State of New Mexico, United States, except where non-excludable law requires otherwise. Disputes may be brought before a court having lawful jurisdiction; this clause does not impose compulsory arbitration or remove mandatory rights to a different forum. No term excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded. Any negotiated commercial liability allocation must be agreed separately.

## 11. Changes and contact

The terms version accepted for your order remains linked to it. New versions apply to new orders unless a change is separately agreed and lawful. We do not treat an earlier payment as acceptance of later terms.

Contact: **Bluefin Tuna LLC — support@bluefintuna.life**. Current business contact details are also available on our Company and Contact pages.

# Bluefin Tuna LLC — Cancellation & Refund Policy

**Version:** service-terms-2026-10-30-v2  
**Effective date:** 2026-10-30  
**Contact:** support@bluefintuna.life

## Scope

This policy applies to our project-planning services and compatible add-ons. It forms part of the accepted Service Terms and order summary. It does not replace Apple’s rules for App Store purchases. Mandatory legal rights take precedence.

## Before work starts

You may request cancellation before substantive project work begins. The normal remedy is a full refund. A third-party expense can be deducted only if it was specifically disclosed, authorized in advance, actually incurred and lawfully non-refundable. We do not automatically deduct our Stripe processing fee from your refund.

Successful payment, opening an automated workspace or merely copying your files does not, by itself, mean that all of the professional work has been performed. We keep a record of substantive work commencement and progress.

## After work starts

You may request cancellation after work has begun. We assess the completed and remaining work against the accepted scope and provide a reasonable, itemized calculation. A deduction must be supported by documented work or separately authorized third-party costs, must not exceed the relevant agreed fee, and remains subject to mandatory rights. We do not apply a blanket “all sales final” rule.

## Missing information or an order we cannot perform

Incomplete inputs may delay the start of work, but do not automatically eliminate cancellation or refund rights. We explain what is missing and offer a practical way to proceed, modify or close the order. If we cannot accept or provide the purchased service, we refund the unperformed portion and provide any additional remedy required by applicable law. If no substantive work has begun and no authorized lawful third-party cost applies, the refund is full.

## Incomplete, corrupted or materially nonconforming deliverables

Contact us with the order reference and a description of the problem. We compare the deliverable with the agreed scope and propose correction, completion, re-delivery or an appropriate refund or price reduction. Correcting a material failure to meet the purchased scope is not automatically charged as an additional revision. This review does not waive any statutory remedy.

A scheduling recommendation you decide not to use, or a project outcome outside the agreed deliverable, is assessed against the actual contract rather than treated as an automatic refund entitlement or an automatic exclusion.

## File expiry and access problems

The 12-hour temporary intake deadline, 30-day final-download availability and 90-day private archive policy are disclosed separately. These technical time limits do not erase legal rights or evidence of your payment. A paid order with expired or unsuccessful intake may be resolved through authorized re-upload without charging again for the same service.

If you report a download failure during the availability period, we provide reasonable secure assistance. Do not send passwords, payment-card details, invitation secrets or unrelated confidential files in a support message. Deleting a project-file archive does not automatically delete billing or consent evidence.

## How to request a refund

Email **support@bluefintuna.life** with your order or invoice reference, the service concerned and your request. We explain the proposed outcome in writing. Any legally applicable response/refund period prevails. We do not promise an arbitrary universal bank-credit date; once a refund is approved, we initiate it promptly through the original payment method where possible and provide its status or reference. The issuer/payment provider controls the subsequent posting time.

We do not ask you to pay an additional fee to release a refund. A change to a different recipient or bank account requires a secure, documented process and is not made on an unverified email instruction.

## Consumer rights and early performance

The standard launch flow is for business/professional orders. If mandatory consumer protections apply to a particular purchase, including withdrawal or cancellation rights, those rights remain applicable. A general terms checkbox is not a substitute for a legally required separate express request for early performance or acknowledgment of the effects of full performance. Such a transaction is reviewed before early work or charging where required.

## Payment disputes

We investigate disputes using the accepted scope, communications, actual work and delivery records. A dispute or suspected duplicate payment may temporarily suspend further work or download authorization while reviewed. We do not rewrite historic consent, impose an automatic penalty, or retain more project data than necessary solely because a concern was raised.

# Bluefin Tuna LLC — Project Portal Privacy Supplement

**Version:** service-terms-2026-10-30-v2  
**Effective date:** 2026-10-30



## 1. Scope and contact

This supplement explains how **Bluefin Tuna LLC** handles information for its planning-service ordering, temporary intake, private workspaces, billing and customer-delivery portal. It supplements, rather than replaces, our existing website and application privacy disclosures. Contact **support@bluefintuna.life** for portal privacy questions or rights requests.

For information we collect to run customer relationships, billing, security and the portal, Bluefin Tuna LLC determines the relevant purposes and means. If a customer asks us to process personal data solely on its instructions within project documents, the parties must determine their respective roles and any required data-processing terms before transfer. The basic portal agreement is not a promise that every regulated or sensitive-data project is suitable.

## 2. Information handled

Depending on the order, we handle customer/contact name, business name, email, billing address, tax identifiers where relevant, project reference and location, selected scope and add-ons, quotes, accepted policy versions, payment and invoice references, project documents, deliverables and support communications.

We keep technical records needed for authorization, payment reconciliation, transfer integrity, permitted downloads, deletion and security. These may include timestamps, file types and sizes, cryptographic checksums, internal order/file identifiers, access/revocation status and error records. Necessary network/security metadata may also be processed by infrastructure providers; we do not promise that no IP address is ever processed.

Stripe processes payment-card details. We do not intentionally store full card numbers or card security codes in our portal database. Do not place financial credentials, passwords, government identifiers or unnecessary personal information in project files.

## 3. Purposes and grounds

We use relevant information to assess and accept orders, determine the agreed scope and applicable billing/tax treatment, collect payment, perform the service, deliver files, provide support, maintain necessary financial/contract records and prevent unauthorized access or fraud.

Where applicable privacy law requires a legal basis, the appropriate basis may include performing or preparing a contract, legal obligations, or legitimate interests such as securing the portal and dealing with business contacts, subject to the applicable balancing and rights requirements. Where consent is required for a particular optional use, it is requested separately. Accepting the Service Terms does not waive privacy rights or authorize unrelated marketing.

## 4. Service providers and access

The principal providers in this service are:

- **Stripe:** payment processing and related receipt, invoice, fraud and transaction functions.
- **Cloudflare:** hosting, access protection, bot verification, temporary R2 file storage and D1 order/operational records.
- **Google Drive:** a private project working repository controlled by our authorized operator, used through a connected account to prepare and retain the purchased work.

The initial working repository uses a personally held Google Drive account with access restricted to the authorized operator and the application's permitted files. This is not a publicly shared customer directory or a guarantee of a particular enterprise Google Workspace contract. We do not claim that a specific data-processing agreement or international-transfer mechanism has been executed unless it has actually been put in place.

Customers obtain approved deliverables through the Bluefin Tuna portal. A Google account is not required, and the customer's ordinary portal response does not expose our Drive OAuth credentials, raw Drive identifiers or public Google sharing URLs.

Authorized staff/advisers may receive necessary information for service performance, support, accounting, security or legal matters. Additional document access is limited to a legitimate need. We do not publish project files as marketing examples without separate permission.

## 5. File lifecycle and retention

| Information | Normal rule |
|---|---|
| R2 temporary intake files | New access ends 12 hours after intake-session creation. Scheduled physical deletion follows; incidents can delay cleanup. |
| Private Drive working files | Retained while the accepted project is being performed. |
| Approved final delivery access | Available for 30 days from final publication, as shown in the portal. |
| Private Drive project/final archive | Scheduled for deletion 90 days from that same final publication time. |
| Project files where an unpublished project is closed | Normally deleted 30 days after written closure unless a shorter lawful period or justified hold applies. |
| Abandoned, unpaid order/contact metadata | Normally removed or minimized 90 days after closure/expiry, excluding a documented security, dispute or legal need. |
| Essential accounting, transaction and agreement evidence | Normally retained under an operational seven-year schedule measured from the end of the calendar year in which the order closes. Only necessary records are retained; applicable legal requirements and documented necessity may require a different period. |
| Routine operational/security logs controlled by us | Normally retained for up to 30 days, except evidence required for a documented incident or legal matter. Provider-managed security logs may follow the provider's applicable arrangements. |

The seven-year business-record schedule is not a representation that every jurisdiction requires exactly seven years. Records are reviewed for necessity and removed or minimized when no longer required. Tax returns, mandatory records and documented disputes can have different preservation requirements; project files are not kept for seven years merely because the invoice is.

Payment and a verified Drive transfer do not extend R2 intake access. Downloading files or opening an invitation does not automatically restart delivery/archive periods. A documented revised publication can have an explicit new date; dates are not silently extended by link reissue. Routine deletion may occur on the next scheduled run rather than at the exact access-expiry second.

Legal holds must identify a purpose and be reviewed; they are not indefinite blanket exceptions. Provider backup/retention behavior can differ from deletion of active objects. We do not promise instant deletion from all third-party backups. A restored backup must not make an expired or revoked customer file publicly downloadable again.

## 6. International processing

Our service is operated internationally. Cloudflare, Google, Stripe, their relevant infrastructure and authorized operators may process information in countries other than the customer's country. Incorporation or payment collection in the United States is not a promise that all processing or storage is exclusively in the United States or in the European Union.

Where applicable law requires particular transfer safeguards, contractual arrangements, location controls or regulated-data protections, those must be addressed before the affected information is accepted. Customers with a strict residency, localization or regulated-data requirement should contact us before upload; the standard portal does not automatically satisfy those requirements.

## 7. Security and your responsibilities

We use private storage, access controls, limited delivery authorization, verification of relevant payment events, format/size restrictions, transfer-integrity checks and a controlled document-review process. Checksums are used to detect byte mismatches; they do not certify that content is free from malicious material. We make no absolute security guarantee.

Keep your portal invitation, passcode and session secure. Share only information you are authorized to provide. Do not upload unrelated sensitive data or executable/macro content not expressly accepted by the service. If access is lost or compromised, contact support rather than sending secrets in ordinary email.

## 8. Your rights and requests

Depending on applicable law, you may have rights to obtain information about processing, access or correct personal data, request deletion or restriction, object to certain uses, obtain portability, or withdraw consent for processing that actually relies on consent. You may also have a right to complain to a competent authority.

We verify requests proportionately and do not automatically ask for a passport or other excessive identification. Some information must be retained for lawful accounting, contractual, security or dispute reasons; where applicable, we explain the relevant limitation. If a project document contains another person's data, the relevant business customer may need to participate in the response.

## 9. Changes

Material changes are published with a new version and effective date. A change to this notice does not silently rewrite the contractual terms accepted for an older order. Existing app-specific disclosures and support/privacy URLs remain applicable to their respective services.
